1. Two objects X and Y are having same masses. Among them the specific heat capacity of X is more, if equal amount of
heat energy is given to both, whose temperature will be more? Why? The temperature of 20 kg water in the radiator of a car
(engine) is 30 °C. If the temperature of the water increases up to 100 °C after the engine is healed, what quantity of heat energy will the water absorb? (Ans: 5.88 x 106 Joule)
Ans:- When equal amounts of heat energy are given to objects X and Y, both having the same mass, the temperature of object
Y becomes higher. This is because object X has a greater specific heat capacity, meaning it needs more heat energy to raise
its temperature by 1°C. Since both receive the same amount of heat, X’s temperature increases less, while Y, which requires
less heat for the same rise, shows a greater increase in temperature. Therefore, Y becomes hotter than X.
Given, Mass of Water (m) = 20kg
Initial temperature(t1) = 30°C
Final temperature (t2) = 100°C
Quantity of heat (Q) = ?
Specific heat capacity of water (s) = 4200J/kg°C Now we know that, Quantity of heat (Q) = msdt = 20*4200* (100-30) =20*4200* 70 = 5.88 x 106 Joule

substance A by 1°C. This value shows how much heat the substance needs to change its temperature. A higher specific heat
capacity means the substance heats up more slowly, while a lower value means it heats up faster.
ii) Which of the above given substance will gain more temperature while heating equal mass of all the three substances
supplied with equal amount of heat? Give reasons.
Ans:- Among the three substances, B will gain the highest temperature because it has the lowest specific heat capacity. Since
it needs less heat to raise its temperature, it heats up more than A and C when the same amount of heat is supplied.
iii) Which will go down more in depth while keeping equal mass of all three substances heated for the same temperature of
100°C and kept on a wax slab and why?
Ans:- Substance A will go down more in depth into the wax slab.
This is because all three substances have the same mass and are heated to the same temperature (100°C), but substance A has
the highest specific heat capacity. A higher specific heat capacity means it stores more total heat energy at the same
temperature, so it transfers more heat to the wax and melts it more, causing it to sink deeper.
4. The boiling temperature of water cannot be measured with help of an alcohol thermometer, why? Calculate the final
temperature of the mixture when 200ml milk 50°C is mixed with 10 ml water at 10°C. Let specific heat capacity of water and
milk is same.(Ans: 48.09°C)
Ans:- The boiling temperature of water cannot be measured with an alcohol thermometer because alcohol boils at a
temperature lower than 100°C. When water reaches its boiling point, the alcohol inside the thermometer would already have
evaporated or boiled, so it cannot accurately show temperatures as high as 100°C.
Given, mass of milk (m1) = 200ml
mass of water (m2) = 10ml
Its temperature milk (t1) = 50°C
temperature of water (t2) = 10°C
Final temperature (t) = ?
Then we know that, heat loss = heat gain
Or, m1*s* dt1 = m2 * s * dt2
Or, 200 * (t1-t) = 10 * (t-t2) (specific heat capacity of water and milk is same.)
Therefore final temperature of mixture will be 48.09°C.
